forecast-period.text: A weak high pressure system centred over NSW will slowly move east while maintaining a ridge over SA until Saturday. A strong cold front will then begin to move into the Bight and move east over the state from late Saturday and throughout Sunday. Another cold front is then forecast to move into the Bight from late Monday.
For latest warnings go to www.bom.gov.au, subscribe to RSS feeds, call 1300 659 210* or listen for warnings on relevant TV and radio broadcasts.
* Calls to 1300 numbers cost around 27.5c incl. GST, higher from mobiles or public phones.

Patchy morning frost and fog on and east of the ranges. Dry in the northeast. Isolated showers developing in the west during the morning, with a slight chance of an isolated thunderstorm about the southwest from the afternoon. Showers extending southeast to reach the eastern districts during the evening. Maximum temperatures above average. Northeast to northwesterly winds, fresh at times over western and central SA during the day and coastal areas during the evening.
Isolated showers about the Southern Agricultural Area easing in later in the evening. East to northeasterly winds.

Dry in the far northeast. Scattered showers across the state, tending to areas of rain about western and central parts from the late afternoon. The chance of an isolated thunderstorm about western and central coastal areas. Maximum temperatures near average in the south, grading to above average in the north. North to northwesterly winds, fresh at times about coastal areas, ahead of a fresh westerly change moving across the state from the evening. Strong and gusty winds possible about the west coast in the evening.

Areas of rain across the state, tending to scattered showers from the west during the day and gradually contracting to the Agricultural Areas from the evening. Possible small hail with showers about the far west coast. Possible isolated thunderstorm about coastal districts. Possible raised dust in the far northeast. Maximum temperatures below average. North to northwesterly winds in the southeast ahead of the change, fresh west to southwesterly winds elsewhere, moderating in the evening and reaching the southeast. Strong and gusty winds possible inland and extending across coastal areas during the day.

text.p: Possible patchy morning frost about the Flinders Ranges and northwest SA. Isolated showers possible about the Agricultural Areas. Maximum temperatures below average. West to northwesterly winds, fresh about windward facing coasts and ranges.

Cumulative rainfall totals to the end of Monday: Less than 2 mm in the far north to northeast. Falls of 5 to 15 mm across much of the state, increasing 15 to 25 mm about the Agricultural Areas, West Coast district and southern pastoral districts. Local falls of 25 to 50 mm are possible across the state and over the ranges.
